title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
description: Ground model answers in your own documents instead of trusting memorized knowledge.

lessons.title: Why RAG, and When Not To
lessons.description: The problem RAG solves, and simpler alternatives that solve it too.
learningObjectives: Compare RAG to fine-tuning and long context
Recognize when RAG is the wrong tool

lessons.title: Chunking Strategy
lessons.description: How you split documents determines what the model can retrieve.
learningObjectives: Chunk by size, structure, and overlap
Avoid chunks that split meaning apart
Attach metadata to chunks for filtering

lessons.title: The Retrieve-then-generate Pipeline
lessons.description: Wire retrieval and generation into one request.
learningObjectives: Retrieve top-k chunks for a query
Assemble a grounded prompt from retrieved chunks
Cite sources in the final answer

lessons.title: Evaluating a RAG System
lessons.description: Know whether your RAG system is actually grounded, not just fluent.
learningObjectives: Check answers are supported by retrieved text
Catch retrieval failures versus generation failures
Build a small RAG evaluation set

assignment.title: Assignment: A Grounded Docs Q&A Tool
assignment.description: Build a real retrieve-then-generate tool over the FAQ corpus from Module 4 — cited answers, an explicit refusal path, and a two-layer eval harness that separates retrieval failures from generation failures.
learningObjectives: Wire retrieval and generation into one grounded, cited pipeline
Refuse to answer when nothing relevant was retrieved
Diagnose retrieval failures separately from generation failures with a real eval set
